python3 - <<'PY'
import io
p='src/index.css'
s=io.open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()

# 1. widen the compact tier to cover tablets
old_q = """@media (max-width: 720px), (max-height: 520px) {"""
new_q = """@media (max-width: 1024px), (max-height: 520px) {"""
assert old_q in s, "compact query not found"
s = s.replace(old_q, new_q)

# 2. the header comment above it needs to match the new reach
old_c = """/* --- phone, portrait or landscape ----------------------------------------
 * Width alone is the wrong trigger. A phone on its side is ~844x390: wide
 * enough to miss a max-width rule, but only 390px tall, and the wrapped bars
 * from the 900px rule above then eat 372px of that — leaving 5% of the screen
 * for the timeline. Short viewports get the same compact treatment as narrow
 * ones, and because this block comes after the 900px one it wins there.
 */"""
new_c = """/* --- phone and tablet ----------------------------------------------------
 * Measured chrome before this block existed, at 100% zoom:
 *
 *    768x1024  iPad portrait    374px  (63% timeline)
 *   1024x768   iPad landscape   383px  (50%)
 *    960x900   half-screen      409px  (55%)
 *    390x844   phone            488px  (42%)
 *    844x390   phone, sideways  372px  ( 5%)
 *
 * So the bars were never a phone-only problem — they stack as soon as their
 * content stops fitting, which is anything under ~1400px. Everything up to a
 * 1024px tablet now collapses to ☰ plus a scrubber.
 *
 * Height is a separate trigger, not a refinement of width: a phone on its side
 * is ~844x390, wide enough to miss any max-width rule but with only 390px to
 * spend. Hence the `max-height` arm.
 */"""
assert old_c in s, "compact comment not found"
s = s.replace(old_c, new_c)

# 3. the old 900px block is now fully shadowed — every property it sets is
#    either overridden or made irrelevant by the compact tier. Drop it.
dead = """@media (max-width: 900px) {
  .topbar { flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px; }
  .topbar__readouts { margin-left: 0; width: 100%; }
  .readout { flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 0; }
  .bottombar { flex-wrap: wrap; }
  .controls { margin-left: 0; width: 100%; }
  .scrub input { width: 100%; flex: 1 1 auto; }
  .scrub { flex: 1 1 100%; }
}

"""
assert dead in s, "900px block not found"
s = s.replace(dead, "")
io.open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
print("compact tier -> 1024px; dead 900px block removed")
PY

git add src/index.css && git restore --staged .specstory 2>/dev/null; git diff --cached --name-only && git commit --quiet --file=- <<'MSG'
feat: extend the compact layout to tablets, and unwrap the bars below 1400px

Measuring the sizes in between showed the stacked bars were never a phone
problem — they stack as soon as their content stops fitting, which is anything
under roughly 1400px:

              before          after
  768x1024    374px  63%      88px  91%    iPad portrait
  1024x768    383px  50%      88px  89%    iPad landscape
   960x900    409px  55%      88px  ~90%   half-screen laptop
  1025x800    225px  72%     190px  76%
  1280x800    193px  76%     157px  80%
  1366x768    191px  75%     157px  ~79%
  1440x900    160px  82%     160px  82%    unchanged

iPad landscape was the worst case in the whole range at 50% — worse than
portrait, and it never matched the old 900px rule at all, so nothing had been
tuned for it.

Everything up to a 1024px tablet now gets the ☰ drawer. Between 1025 and
1399 the bars stay but stop wrapping into second rows: the bottom bar loses
the nowrap "click any card" hint (~300px, and the drawer still carries that
sentence where touch users need it) and the top bar loses the strapline, whose
46ch allowance was what pushed the row over. Both return at 1440, where the
full layout fits as designed.

The bottom bar still wraps between 1025 and 1279. Unwrapping it there would
mean hiding the category labels and shipping icon-only filters, which trades
clarity and the buttons' accessible names for 33px — not worth it.

The old 900px block is deleted rather than left in place: the compact tier now
covers everything it did, so every rule in it was dead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <<EMAIL_REDACTED>>
